I give up. I could not finish the proof, so `/work/putnam_2025_b6.lean` is unchanged and still contains the `sorry`.

The answer 1/4 is right, and the lower bound is done. The witness g(n) = n² gives g(g(n))^(1/4) = n ≤ (n+1)² − n² = 2n+1. I checked this in a scratch file, `/work/scratch_lower.lean`, and it compiles with no errors or `sorry`. Note that this check covers only the lower bound.

The missing part is the upper bound: for every r > 1/4, no g can satisfy the condition. I did not find a complete argument for it. The growth heuristics I tried show that any solution must be roughly polynomial, with g(n) ≈ n^a forcing a²r ≤ a−1. For r > 1/4 that inequality has no solution, which matches the answer. However, I could not turn this into a rigorous, formalizable argument, because the constraints only bound g from below and the needed upper bounds did not follow.
